subject.title: [Bug]: Secret provider crash-loop exhausts 1Password service account rate limits

question: What startup SecretRef failure policy should OpenClaw use to prevent supervised restart loops from amplifying side-effecting external secret-provider calls?
rationale: This choice affects fail-closed credential handling, operator recovery, external secret-provider side effects, and whether OpenClaw should retry, degrade, or delegate caching to provider-owned resolvers.

options.title: Generic repair safe mode
options.body: After repeated startup SecretRef failures, start a repairable control plane without automatically resolving side-effecting provider refs again, and require explicit operator reload/start after repair.

options.title: Bounded startup retry only
options.body: Add a small generic startup retry/backoff around SecretRef activation, accepting that permanent failures can still restart and consume provider calls more slowly.

options.title: Resolver/plugin delegation only
options.body: Document Varlock/ClawHub-style resolver plugins and supervisor guidance while leaving core startup fail-fast semantics unchanged.

recommendation.title: Generic repair safe mode
recommendation.body: After repeated startup SecretRef failures, start a repairable control plane without automatically resolving side-effecting provider refs again, and require explicit operator reload/start after repair.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest feature-history signal for the SecretRef runtime and eager activation contract is joshavant's external-secrets work.
